assessment: Lu et al. provide a powerful statistical method that measures excess sharing of de novo mutations between pairs of disorders. This method extends the concept of 'genetic correlation' to disorders caused by de-novo mutations, measuring the correlation in excess de-novo mutations in genome-wide genes for different classes of mutations. The authors apply the method to nine disorders including a developmental disorder, autism spectrum disorder, congenital heart disease, schizophrenia, and intellectual disability, finding a statistically significant overlap between 12 pairs of disorders in de novo mutations that cause a loss of gene function. This method will be of interest to researchers working on disorders caused by de-novo mutations.
